newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 20.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
- U.S. housing starts fell 5.1 percent in October.
- Sony Corp is considering a public stock sale for its Sony Pictures Entertainment unit.
- General Motors Corp is slow in shipping new car and truck models to its dealerships.

- The scandal over taped recordings of senior executives at Texaco Inc speaking poorly of blacks has brought attention to the resentments underlying the promotion of equal opportunity in corporate America.
- The former executive at Texaco Inc who divulged recordings of other senior officials talking horribly about black employees has been charged with obstructing justice.
- An investment adviser from Tenfly, N.J. has pleaded guilty of stealing more than $65 million from clients in a fraud scheme.
- Georgia state's utility company Oglethorpe Power Corp has reached a deal with power marketer LG & E Energy Corp to supply half of its electricity needs.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton's Administration expects two meetings during the next month to set the stage for a global agreement abolishing tariffs on computer and software products.
- The Sumitomo Corp announced a loss of $1.9 billion for the first six months of its fiscal year as a result of huge losses from illegal copper trading.
- Mama Tisch's Italian Specialties initial public offering is in trouble.
